channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Offers Up to 173,000 Tenge State Subsidy for Housing Deposits
item.description: Kazakhstanis have until the end of December to top up their housing deposits with Otbasy Bank and receive a state subsidy of up to 173,000 tenge. The subsidy amounts to 20% of housing savings, capped at 200 monthly calculated indicators (MRPs). The maximum state payout is 173,000 tenge per depositor.

item.title: Germany Proposes EU Law Requiring AI Companies to Pay for Media Content
item.description: The German government has proposed an EU mechanism requiring generative AI providers to pay rights holders for content created by their systems. This aims to compensate media outlets whose content is used for AI training, potentially impacting advertising and subscription revenues. The proposal seeks to ensure fair remuneration for publishers.

item.title: Uzbek Cotton Clusters Receive Debt Deferral Worth 4.4 Trillion Soums
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved measures to enhance the competitiveness of its light industry. Cotton-textile clusters will receive a deferral on 3.2 trillion soums of debt for cotton harvests from 2022-2023, with repayment extended to 2028-2029. An additional 1.2 trillion soums debt for the 2025 cotton harvest is also deferred until March 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan Hospitals Face High Occupancy Due to Seasonal Respiratory Illnesses
item.description: Infectious disease wards in Kazakhstan are at 68% occupancy, with pediatric beds at 72%, as of November 25. The West Kazakhstan and Mangystau regions report the highest bed occupancy. Additional beds have been deployed in 13 regions to manage the surge in cases, with over 1.5 million ORVI cases reported since the start of the epidemic season.

item.title: Almaty Court Sentences Civil Activist Sanzhar Bokeyev to Ten Years for Fraud
item.description: The Almaly District Court in Almaty has sentenced civil activist Sanzhar Bokeyev to ten years in prison. He was found guilty of large-scale fraud, money laundering, theft, illegal logging, and spreading false information. His nephew received a six-and-a-half-year sentence but was released due to statute of limitations.

item.title: Vice-Rector of Satbayev University Detained on Corruption Charges in Almaty
item.description: Yerzhan Kuldeev, the Vice-Rector of Satbayev University, has been detained in Almaty on suspicion of multiple corruption offenses. The General Prosecutor's Office of Kazakhstan is investigating the case, with a court ordering the detention of Kuldeev and other individuals involved. Information about Kuldeev's detention first surfaced in late September 2026.

item.title: Former Nur Otan Ideologue Sanjar Bokayev Sentenced to 10 Years for Corruption
item.description: Sanjar Bokayev, a former ideologue for the Nur Otan party, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison by an Almaty court. He was found guilty of embezzlement, money laundering, organizing theft, illegal tree felling, and spreading false information. The court also banned him from media and public activities for ten years. The verdict is not yet final.

item.title: Almaty Restaurateurs Welcome Simplified Rules for Summer Terraces
item.description: The Association of Restaurateurs of Kazakhstan has welcomed updated regulations for summer terraces in Almaty. New rules simplify the approval process, reducing administrative burdens and costs for businesses. Previously, obtaining permits was time-consuming and expensive. The changes allow terraces to be classified as landscaping elements, not requiring land ownership, making it easier for establishments to expand seating for the warm season.

item.title: Tashkent Proposes International Guidelines for AI in Tourism
item.description: Tashkent is initiating the development of international approaches for the responsible use of artificial intelligence in tourism and training new specialists. A key outcome of the 'AI and Tourism' forum, held in Tashkent, is a document with recommendations for safe, ethical, and effective AI implementation. This document will be submitted to UN Tourism and other relevant international organizations.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Addresses Public Transport Concerns and Plans Upgrades
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with investors to discuss improving public transport services. He acknowledged public dissatisfaction, particularly with Tashkent's metro congestion. Plans include introducing new metro trains and upgrading existing ones to enhance passenger experience by the end of next year.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Update Water Strategy Until 2040 Following New Water Code Adoption
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is set to update its National Water Strategy until 2040, aligning it with the recently adopted Water Code. The government is also improving coordination for water resource monitoring to ensure accurate data on water reserves, usage, and losses, crucial for economic development and security.

item.title: Nearly 5 Kilograms of Drugs Found in Vehicle on Balykchy-Kazarman Highway
item.description: Authorities in Kyrgyzstan's Naryn region seized nearly 5 kilograms of drugs from a vehicle on the Balykchy-Kazarman highway. The driver and passengers tested positive for drug use. Investigations revealed additional drugs and a firearm at suspects' residences, leading to one arrest and detention.

item.title: Halyk Bank Facilitates $1.5 Billion Loan for 'Altynalmas' Acquisition
item.description: Halyk Bank has organized a $1.5 billion syndicated loan provided by five Kazakhstani banks to fund the acquisition of shares in the gold mining company 'Altynalmas'. The loan is for a company owned by Shakhmyrat Mutalip, a businessman also linked to Forbes. The deal involved only commercial banks.

item.title: Kazakhstan Boxers Learn Opponents at World Cup Finals in Tashkent
item.description: The draw for the final stage of the World Boxing-2026 World Cup took place in Tashkent. Kazakhstan's national team, comprising eleven athletes, discovered their initial opponents. Eight boxers will start from the quarterfinals, while three have advanced directly to the semifinals, securing at least bronze medals.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prepares Railways for China-Kyrgyzstan Route Launch
item.description: Uzbekistan is preparing its railways for increased cargo traffic following the launch of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan route. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stated that cargo volume is projected to increase tenfold to 15-16 million tons annually. The country plans to build 545 km of new lines and electrify 65% of its network by 2030.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Attends AI Conference in Russia, Discusses Trade
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Vladimir Putin in Russia, attending an AI conference. Tokayev emphasized Kazakhstan's strategic partnership with Russia, noting progress in mutual trade reaching $28 billion in 2025, with 96% of transactions in roubles or tenge. Kazakhstan plans to phase out 3G by 2027.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Increasing Height Limit for Ventilated Facades to 75 Meters
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Construction proposes increasing the maximum height for buildings using ventilated facade systems without special technical conditions from 66 to 75 meters. The draft amendment to construction rules is based on results from seismic resistance tests. It also clarifies requirements for facade system components and wind load calculations.

item.title: Two Teenagers Sentenced to Five Years in Astana for Robbery and Other Crimes
item.description: A specialized inter-district juvenile court in Astana has sentenced two teenagers to five years in prison each for a series of crimes including robbery, fraud, hooliganism, and theft. The total damage to victims exceeded 3 million tenge. The court found they had committed multiple offenses between March and June, including assaulting individuals and stealing phones.

item.title: Kazakhstan AI Startup Pulsar.ai Targets Chinese Automakers with SmartRail Scanner
item.description: Kazakhstani startup Pulsar.ai is seeking to enter the Chinese market with its AI-powered SmartRail vehicle scanner, which identifies vehicle damage and wear. The company trained its AI models using 150,000 images from a pilot project with Astana Motors. Founder Baglan Olzhabayev believes Kazakhstan's climate offers a competitive advantage.

item.title: Kazakh Activist Sanjar Bokayev Sentenced to Ten Years in Prison
item.description: Kazakh public figure Sanjar Bokayev has been sentenced to ten years in prison by the Almalinsky District Court in Almaty. His associate, Madiyar Kalmenov, received six years and six months, while videographer Ulan Nusipkozha was given two years and six months of freedom restriction. Bokayev denies guilt, calling the case fabricated.

item.title: Gender Equality Initiatives Assessed at Regional Competition in Uzbekistan
item.description: Initiatives aimed at empowering women, protecting their rights, and increasing their participation were evaluated at a regional competition in Uzbekistan. Organized by the Senate of Oliy Majlis and the Committee for Women and Family, the event featured projects from 5 regional and 22 district/city organizations. Key focus areas included women's socio-political activity, leadership roles, and digital literacy.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Activist Sanzhar Bokaev Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison
item.description: Social activist Sanzhar Bokaev, known for his anti-utility fee initiatives, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison in Almaty. His nephew received six years and six months, and his former videographer two years and six months. Bokaev was found guilty on four counts, including large-scale fraud and spreading false information. He denied the charges.

item.title: Kazatomprom Board Assures Investors Amidst Management Resignations and Corruption Probe
item.description: The Board of Directors of Kazatomprom has addressed shareholders, clients, and partners following the departure of three board members and the detention of one on corruption charges. The board acknowledged potential investor concerns, pledged to address internal control weaknesses, and is cooperating with authorities. Operational activities and strategic plans remain unaffected.

item.title: BI Group's Construction Arm Recommends 25 Billion Tenge Dividend Payout
item.description: BI Development Ltd.'s board of directors has recommended a dividend payout of 25 billion tenge from profits for the first nine months of 2025. The net profit for this period was 81.93 billion tenge. The final decision rests with the shareholders' general meeting. The dividends will be distributed among various group structures.

item.title: New 300-Capacity Special Needs Kindergarten Opens in Aktobe, Funded by Returned Assets
item.description: A new 300-capacity special needs kindergarten, 'Samğau', has opened in Aktobe, Kazakhstan. Built using assets returned to the state, it aims to alleviate kindergarten shortages and improve support for children with special educational needs. The facility cost 7.8 billion tenge and was inaugurated ahead of the 35th anniversary of Kazakhstan's independence.

item.title: South Korean University INHA Plans to Open Campus in Margilan, Uzbekistan
item.description: South Korea's INHA University, a leading institution in engineering and technology, plans to establish a new campus in Margilan, Uzbekistan. A delegation led by the Chongseok Foundation chairman and INHA University president met with Fergana region officials to discuss educational partnerships and joint projects. The campus will focus on artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and engineering, aiming to enhance higher education quality and IT potential in the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan Wins Top Prize at International 'Green Skills Award 2026'
item.description: Uzbekistan's project 'Sustainable Future Society' (SFS) secured first place at the international 'Green Skills Award 2026', organized by the European Training Foundation (ETF). Announced in Turin, Italy, the project outperformed 368 other entries from 94 countries. SFS originated from a school initiative addressing waste sorting and evolved into an environmental movement led by students, adapting the Eco-Schools methodology.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Teenager dies from antibiotic test, raising drug safety concerns
item.description: A 14-year-old boy in Almaty died after an antibiotic test, prompting renewed questions about drug safety and the monitoring of adverse reactions in Kazakhstan. The incident highlights the potential for severe side effects, including anaphylactic shock, even from prescribed medications.

item.title: Astana residents can find their polling stations for upcoming city council elections
item.description: Astana residents can determine their polling station location in advance through the official website sailau.astana.kz, the 'Saylau Astana' Telegram chatbot, or by calling the iKomek hotline. Voters must bring identification on election day, November 29.

item.title: Sanzhar Bokaev detained on suspicion of spreading false information
item.description: Sanzhar Bokaev has been detained on suspicion of spreading false information and creating negative public opinion through social media videos, according to the Prosecutor General's Office of Kazakhstan. The specific details of the alleged false information were not immediately disclosed.

item.title: Ulaanbaatar street to be named after Manas, Kyrgyz epic hero
item.description: A street in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, is planned to be named in honor of Manas, the hero of the Kyrgyz national epic. The decision was made during a meeting between Bishkek and Ulaanbaatar city officials, symbolizing historical memory and friendship between the two nations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Completes Reclamation of Former Uranium Sites Yangiabad and Chorkesar-2
item.description: Uzbekistan has announced the completion of environmental restoration work at the former uranium sites of Yangiabad and Chorkesar-2. The project, supported by the EU and EBRD with 9 million euros, aimed to reduce radiation and environmental risks. Additional sites require further funding.

item.title: Almaty Court Sentences Activist Sanzhar Bokeyev to 10 Years for Fraud and Other Charges
item.description: Almaty's Almaly District Court has sentenced activist Sanzhar Bokeyev to 10 years in prison. He was convicted of fraud, money laundering, theft, illegal logging, and spreading false information. Two co-defendants received prison and restricted freedom sentences.

item.title: Afghan Migrant Families Return from Pakistan Amid Economic Hardship
item.description: An increasing number of Afghan families are returning to Afghanistan from Pakistan as winter approaches, citing economic difficulties and a desire for greater security. Returnees express happiness to be back in their homeland, despite facing hardship, and call for improved facilities and living conditions for migrants. They emphasize a preference for their own country regardless of circumstances.

item.title: Uzbekistan Seeks International Investment and Tourism Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan hosted its First International Investment Forum in Tourism alongside the 31st Tashkent International Tourism Fair. Discussions focused on attracting foreign hotel chains, modernizing accommodation, increasing foreign investment, and strengthening partnerships with international operators. The presence of global hotel brands is seen as boosting the hospitality industry, national economy, and the country's tourism image.

item.title: EU and Turkmenistan Partner to Streamline Caspian Sea Cargo Transport
item.description: Turkmenistan will collaborate with German and French agencies to reduce waiting times and improve ferry schedules at the port of Turkmenbashi. This partnership aims to simplify customs procedures and enhance the efficiency of the Middle Corridor, a key transport route between Central Asia and Europe. The initiative includes exploring a single electronic platform for shipping companies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Agricultural Census Uncovers Unregistered Households
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's agricultural census identified 27,447 households previously missing from official land registry maps. The census, conducted digitally from March 20 to April 10, 2026, recorded a total of 1,333,302 agricultural entities, predominantly personal subsidiary and peasant farms. The largest numbers of households were registered in Osh, Jalal-Abad, and Chuy regions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes Biopharmaceutical Production Complex for Vaccines and Cancer Drugs
item.description: Uzbekistan has opened the CAT BioTech scientific-production complex, the first in Central Asia to offer a full cycle of biotechnological production from laboratory research to finished drug formulation. The facility will focus on producing biological drugs, including flu vaccines and trastuzumab for cancer treatment, aiming to make them more accessible.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Three-Year Credit Holidays for Textile Businesses
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Mirziyoyev has approved measures to boost the textile industry's competitiveness. Companies will receive a three-year "credit holiday" on loan repayments for investment projects and working capital. The initiative aims to increase exports, create jobs, and support businesses with stable economic performance.

item.title: Bishkek Coal Markets Operating with Sufficient Supply and Set Prices
item.description: Coal markets in Bishkek are functioning regularly, with various types of coal available. Prices for "Kara-Keche" coal range from 7,000 to 7,200 soms per ton, while other types like "Shabyrkul" and "Min-Kush" are priced higher. Municipal authorities are monitoring supply and price compliance.
